profilePeriod: Premiership 1983–1991, interpreted alongside explicitly identified later public positions through 2017.
scopeNote: Answers are editorial simulations of documented political principles, not a questionnaire completed by the person. Brazil-specific statements are interpreted in the analogous home-country context. Modern hypothetical technologies require inference.

uncertainties: This is a career profile, not a frozen 1991 snapshot: marriage equality (2017), voluntary assisted dying (2016), and nuclear advocacy (2016) are later positions.
The 1979 proposal to abolish states was repeated in 2016; his constitutional respect and cooperative federalism in office describe implementation constraints, not abandonment of that preference.
Agnosticism is explicitly distinguished from atheism and from hostility to Christian ethics.
Harm minimisation and treatment do not establish endorsement of unrestricted adult drug legalisation; mixed bundled statements are treated cautiously.

No direct positions established for cryptocurrency, facial recognition, modern gender terminology, cultured meat or enhancement implants. These are bounded simulations from documented civil-liberties, equality and research principles, not claimed quotations.
His personal abortion account supports moral permissibility in some circumstances, not an inferred universal gestational policy.
The National Archives page mistakenly labels the external-affairs power as section 52; no section number from that page is repeated in the profile.
distinctions: Unlike a generic collectivist Labour profile, Hawke supported a floating currency, competition and partial bank privatisation.
Unlike a laissez-faire liberal, Hawke retained Medicare, collective wage coordination and a social safety net.
Unlike an isolationist or absolute pacifist, he backed the US alliance and UN-authorised force against Iraq; unlike a militarist, he pursued arms control and negotiated settlements.
The coexistence of conservation and later nuclear support is retained rather than treating environmental concern as rejection of technology.

similarityReview.reason: Both models describe democratic mixed economies and multicultural societies. Hawke differs from the existing Obama vector on estrutura (27.1 vs 40.0), reflecting his explicit proposal to abolish states but strengthen local government; controle (49.7 vs 63.7) and comercio (19.9 vs 28.7) reflect finance deregulation and tariff reductions alongside wage coordination. These are model distinctions supported by Hawke-specific sources, not claims of measured historical distances. The independently authored answers were retained without changes to reduce similarity.
